newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 22.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NATION
- A member of the IMF mission has hinted that Pakistan stands a good chance of getting a $1.5 billion low interest long-term loan in the coming months.
THE NEWS
- Chief Justice of Pakistan Syed Sajjad Ali Shah stopped execution of a death sentence to a murder convict and accepted a review petition filed by his mother.
THE MUSLIM
- The First Women Bank will be privatised in 1997.
- Japan wants both India and Pakistan to refrain from nuclear arms race in the region.
- Businessmen in the industrial city of Faisalabad observed a strike against sectarian killings in the city.
DAWN
- Seventeen people were killed and three injured in Karachi due to heavy rains.

- The federal cabinet again deferred a decision on downsizing government departments and organisations after partially discussing the matter that was placed on its agenda for the third consecutive time.

- Trading volume at the Karachi Stock Exchange soared to a record 209 million shares on account of massive foreign buying enabling the index to cross the psychological barrier of 1,900 points to 1,912.45.
- Japanese foreign minister Yukihiko Ikeda arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday, to hold talks with Pakistani authorities to further improve cooperation in all spheres of common interest.
- The International Monetary Fund's director for Middle East Paul Chabrier arrived in Islamabad to conclude discussions with Pakistani officials for a new medium-term loan.
- The government is preparing an off-shore oil and gas exploration policy carrying appropriate incentives required to attract foreign investment in the sector.

- Pharmaceuticals firm High Noon Laboratories has decided to raise its paid-up capital by 27.42 million rupees to 100 million rupees through the issue of 2.742 million 10-rupee shares to unnamed local and foreign strategic investors.
- The state-run National Bank of Pakistan cut its interest rate by one percent to 5.84 percent charged on different categories of loans.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange said it would place 134 companies on defaulters' counter from August 6, 1997.
- The commissioning of the Ghazi Barotha hydel power project is expected to be delayed by about 12 months.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- A farmers association announced in Lahore it would suspend supply of all agriculture products from July 25 to 27 to major cities and towns of the Punjab province to protest levy of the agriculture income tax by the provincial government.

- Revenues of the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd could increase by 2.21 billion rupees between July-December 1997 from a proposed 150 percent rise in monthly line rental charges and planned new 900,000 connections.
- The state's Board of Investment will announce an investment and industrialisation policy in August, aiming at attracting strategic private investors in the country.
- The state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan has decided to auction 493 tonnes of RBD palm oil from its stocks on July 23.
FINANCIAL POST
- The state's Privatisation Commission has invited financial advisors for restructuring and privatisation of the state-run Pakistan Railways.
- The government has decided to liberalise integrated infrastructural development projects for import of liquified petroleum gas.
